chief_complaint: severe burning, tingling, and hypersensitivity in feet bilaterally with balance instability and loss of proprioception (Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy)
hpi_details: 70F with 20-year history of Type 2 Diabetes presents to rehabilitation clinic with 3-year progression of numbness, burning pain, and `pins and needles` sensation starting in the soles of both feet and gradually moving upward to mid-calf level (`stocking distribution`). Pain is worst at night when bedsheets touch her feet (allodynia). Recently has felt very unsteady on her feet when getting out of bed in the dark or walking on uneven grass, reporting feeling like she is `walking on cotton balls or foam cushions.` Has suffered two un-witnessed falls in her hallway at night over the past month.
ideas: frustrated by burning foot pain preventing restful sleep and terrified of falling and breaking her hip
concerns: worried her feet will turn black and require amputation like her uncle
expectations: wants nerve pain medication, balance physical therapy, and protective footwear advice
medications: Metformin 1000mg BID, Glipizide 10mg daily, Lisinopril 20mg daily

clinical_knowledge.topic: Chronic Diabetic Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy (DSPN) with Neuropathic Pain, Loss of Protective Sensation (LOPS), and Sensory Ataxia leading to high fall risk evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Chronic Diabetic Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy (DSPN) with Neuropathic Pain, Loss of Protective Sensation (LOPS), and Sensory Ataxia leading to high fall risk is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes neuropathic pain pharmacotherapy, fall-prevention balance rehabilitation, and protective footwear to prevent ulceration, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe burning, tingling, and hypersensitivity in feet bilaterally with balance instability and loss of proprioception (Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy)

Key HPI features: 70F with 20-year history of Type 2 Diabetes presents to rehabilitation clinic with 3-year progression of numbness, burning pain, and `pins and needles` sensation starting in the soles of both feet and gradually moving upward to mid-calf level (`stocking distribution`). Pain is worst at night when bedsheets touch her feet (allodynia). Recently has felt very unsteady on her feet when getting out of bed in the dark or walking on uneven grass, reporting feeling like she is `walking on cotton balls or foam cushions.` Has suffered two un-witnessed falls in her hallway at night over the past month.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 74, BP 138/80. Lower extremity neurological and podiatric exam reveals: 1. Sensory: complete absence of protective sensation bilaterally when tested with the Semmes-Weinstein 10-gram (5.07) monofilament across the plantar metatarsal heads, great toes, and heels. Vibration sense (128 Hz tuning fork) and joint position sense (proprioception at the great toe interphalangeal joints) are severely impaired bilaterally up to the ankles. 2. Reflexes: bilateral Achilles tendon reflexes are completely absent (0/4); patellar reflexes diminished (1+). 3. Motor/Balance: Romberg sign is strongly POSITIVE (patient stands stable with eyes open, but immediately sways and loses balance when eyes are closed because of profound large-fiber peripheral sensory loss). Gait demonstrates wide-based, cautious, sensory ataxic steps. Skin inspection shows dry, anhidrotic skin with calluses over the metatarsal heads, intact peripheral pulses, and no active ulcers.
Relevant background/PMH: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (HbA1c 8.2%), Hypertension
Current medications: Metformin 1000mg BID, Glipizide 10mg daily, Lisinopril 20mg daily
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Chronic Diabetic Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy (DSPN) with Neuropathic Pain, Loss of Protective Sensation (LOPS), and Sensory Ataxia leading to high fall risk.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe progressive motor deficit.
management_principles: Neuropathic pain management: initiate first-line pharmacological therapy: Duloxetine (SNRI, starting 30 mg PO daily, advancing to 60 mg) OR Pregabalin (50 mg TID) OR Gabapentin (titrating to 300-600 mg TID)

Fall prevention & Balance rehabilitation: refer to PM&R Physical Therapy for balance/proprioceptive retraining, gait training, vestibular compensation strategies, and assistive device evaluation (prescribe a four-wheeled rollator walker with seat to widen base of support and prevent falls)
Podiatric orthotic protection: prescribe custom-molded diabetic extra-depth therapeutic footwear with pressure-relieving plastazote insoles to prevent neuropathic foot ulceration
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.assessment: Chronic Diabetic Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy (DSPN) with Neuropathic Pain, Loss of Protective Sensation (LOPS), and Sensory Ataxia leading to high fall risk.
reference_soap.plan: Assess for active foot injury or ulceration and recent fall-related injury, and arrange prompt evaluation when present. Use rehabilitation-led balance, gait, home-safety, and assistive-device assessment to reduce falls. Neuropathic-pain medicines may be considered one at a time after renal function, fall/sedation risk, interactions, and patient goals are reviewed. Arrange podiatric foot-risk assessment and appropriately protective footwear when indicated; reinforce daily visual foot inspection and diabetes management with the treating team.

learning_objectives: Perform standardized screening for Loss of Protective Sensation (LOPS) utilizing the Semmes-Weinstein 10-gram monofilament at 10 plantar sites combined with 128 Hz tuning fork vibration testing
Explain the neurophysiology of sensory ataxia and the positive Romberg sign resulting from large-myelinated peripheral sensory fiber loss and impaired joint proprioception

Select evidence-based first-line pharmacological treatments for diabetic neuropathic pain (Duloxetine, Pregabalin, Gabapentin, or Tricyclic Antidepressants) while monitoring side effect profiles in the elderly
Formulate a comprehensive PM&R fall-prevention and ulcer-prevention strategy integrating balance physical therapy, assistive walking devices, and custom-molded diabetic footwear

teaching.one_liner: Physical medicine presentation involving severe burning, tingling, and hypersensitivity in feet bilaterally with balance instability and loss of proprioception (Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy).

must_ask.say: When did the numbness and burning start, and did it begin in your feet before moving up your legs?
How long have you had diabetes, and how well controlled has your blood sugar been?
Have you felt unsteady on your feet or had any falls, especially in the dark?

must_ask.objective: Loss of protective sensation / foot screening
must_ask.say: Have you noticed any sores, cuts, or wounds on your feet that you didn't feel happen?
Is the pain worse at night, even when something light like your bedsheet touches your feet?
